summary: Turn key/value pairs into a lookup object.
documentation: Object.fromEntries consumes an iterable of key/value pairs to construct a new object. Repeated keys are assigned repeatedly, so a later pair replaces an earlier value for that key. This reverses the common Object.entries representation.
inputs: An iterable whose elements each provide a key and a value.
returns: A new object with properties from the supplied pairs.
caution: Duplicate keys lose earlier values. Decide whether that overwrite policy fits your data before using it.
scenarios: Convert form entries into a plain object before local validation.
Build a settings lookup from an exported list of pairs.
Reassemble selected entries after filtering a configuration object.
title: Apply settings in order
problem: Input is an array of [stringKey, value] pairs. Return an object using the last value for each repeated key. Preserve false, zero and null values.
goal: Use Object.fromEntries() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Build the object directly from the pairs; later assignments win.
